items.title: Milgram's obedience rate
items.claim: In Stanley Milgram's 1963 baseline experiment, participants were ordered to deliver what they believed were increasing electric shocks to a stranger. What proportion went all the way to the maximum 450 volts?
items.reveal_title: Around 65% continued to the maximum level
items.reveal:
In Milgram's original Yale study (1963), 26 of 40 participants (65%) continued to the 450V switch under verbal pressure from the experimenter.

Replications, including Burger (2009) in modified form, found broadly similar obedience patterns.
items.why: Situational pressure from a perceived authority figure can override personal moral judgement to a degree most people predict incorrectly.

items.title: What split-brain patients reveal
items.claim: Roger Sperry's split-brain research (Nobel Prize 1981) studied patients whose corpus callosum had been severed to treat what condition?
items.reveal_title: The surgery was a last-resort epilepsy treatment
items.reveal:
Commissurotomy was performed to prevent seizures from spreading between hemispheres. Sperry and Gazzaniga then used these patients to study hemispheric specialisation in the 1960s and 70s.

The research showed each hemisphere could process information independently when communication was cut.
items.why: Some of the most important findings about the brain came from rare clinical populations.

items.title: Re-evaluating Stanford Prison
items.claim: Philip Zimbardo's 1971 Stanford Prison Experiment is often cited as proof that situations dictate behaviour. What did later archival work by Le Texier and others reveal?

options.text: Guards received explicit coaching, undermining the 'natural' interpretation
No participant played the guard role

items.reveal_title: Guards were coached, not spontaneously behaving
items.reveal:
Le Texier's 2018 archival analysis and a 2019 American Psychologist article showed guards received briefings encouraging tough behaviour.

The BBC Prison Study (Reicher & Haslam, 2006) produced very different dynamics under similar setup.
items.why: Replication and archival work reshape how landmark findings are interpreted.
